Background The Regional Programme for Africa is a flagship continental programme of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), implemented through the Regional Service Center for Africa (RSCA), designed to respond to the evolving challenges and opportunities across African. It is anchored in the African Union (AU) Agenda 2063, including its Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan, and aligned with the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029. The programme complements national development efforts by leveraging regional institutions, partnerships and platforms to address transboundary challenges, unlock shared opportunities and scale impact. The Africa Facility to Support Inclusive Transitions (AFSIT), a flagship joint initiative of the African Union Commission (AUC) and UNDP, was established in response to the call made by the AU Heads of State and Government during the 16th Extraordinary Session on Terrorism and Unconstitutional Change of Government (UCG) in Africa, held on May 28, 2023, in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea. The Heads of State and Government called for collective action and solidarity to develop robust response mechanisms to UCGs, deepening democracy, and collective security on the continent. AFSIT provides integrated programmatic support to countries navigating complex political transitions. The Facility adopts a development-oriented approach aimed at strengthening governance structures, promoting stability, and building resilience, ensuring that transitions are peaceful and sustainable. It places strong emphasis on inclusivity, empowering civil society organizations (CSOs) and amplifying the leadership and meaningful participation of women, youth, and marginalized groups in political processes and decision-making. AFSIT also plays a vital role in knowledge development, generating insights and best practices to inform decision-making and strengthen transition processes across the continent. Position Purpose The Programme Analyst will report to the AFSIT Programme Specialist within the UNDP Regional Service Centre for Africa (RSCA) and work closely with UNDP Country Offices, regional institutions, and development partners involved in programme implementation. In Particular The Programme Analyst Will Lead The Delivery Of The Following Projects Under AFSIT Building Resilience and Inclusive Development for Governance and Equality (BRIDGE), which aims to promote gender-responsive, transparent and accountable governance systems while advancing women’s leadership and participation in decision-making processes. Implemented in Guinea-Bissau, South Sudan and The Gambia. Rebuilding the Social Contract Between States and Citizens in the Sahel, which seeks to strengthen inclusive governance and foster renewed trust between citizens and state institutions through dialogue, civic participation, and policy engagement in transition contexts. Implemented in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger. The Programme Analyst will contribute to the implementation of broader AFSIT programme activities, including country-level support, regional initiatives, and knowledge development workstreams. The Programme Analyst will also provide support to wider initiatives under the Regional Programme for Africa, as directed. UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration. review_candidates.title: Principal, Design Office
review_candidates.description: Role Overview Every major project decision depends on accurate engineering information. As our Principal Design Office Lead, you will own the 3D models and engineering drawings for a portfolio of mining growth projects across multiple countries. You will make sure our teams can trust what is on screen matches what is on site. By closing information gaps, verifying designs and holding consultants to high standards, you will help cut rework, avoid delays and reduce project risk. This is a chance to build the digital foundation that our future mines will be designed, built and run on. Key Responsibilities Own the master register of 3D models, drawings, laser scans and engineering data for every mine in the portfolio. Assess the accuracy and completeness of existing information, and prioritise and close the most critical gaps. Verify drawings and models against laser scans, surveys and real site conditions, resolving discrepancies with mine teams and engineers. Plan and coordinate laser scanning and site surveys, and combine scan data with design models into coordinated master models. Lead clash detection and model reviews across civil, structural, mechanical, piping, process and instrumentation disciplines. Support safe, practical and cost-effective designs through constructability, access, maintenance and tie-in reviews on operating sites. Set the CAD, modelling, data and handover standards that consultants and contractors must follow. Check consultant drawings, models and data for quality, raise non-conformances and confirm fixes before accepting deliverables. Keep master records controlled and up to date, and manage as-built handover to operations and asset management teams. Coach draughting and document control staff, and partner with digital technology teams on software and tools. Required Qualifications Diploma or recognised qualification in engineering draughting, drawing office practice or an engineering discipline (or accepted equivalent). At least 10 years of experience in mining, mineral processing or heavy industry, including at least 5 years in 3D CAD modelling. Experience building Building Information Modelling (BIM) or digital twin models that link asset geometry with engineering data. Experience with parametric design tools and data-centric design environments using consistent asset identifiers. Proven experience checking the quality of consultant-produced engineering deliverables. Advanced skills in CAD, model review and point-cloud software, such as AutoCAD, MicroStation, Navisworks, Leica Cyclone or Faro Scene. Preferred Experience Experience on the owner’s side of projects, overseeing engineering consultants and contractors. Experience on brownfields capital projects (upgrades and expansions at operating sites). Experience working in multinational teams. Skills And Competencies Exceptional attention to detail and strong spatial reasoning. Sound judgement and the ability to prioritise logically. Clear communication and the ability to influence across mines, disciplines and cultures. A collaborative approach, knowing when to refer design decisions to responsible engineers. Working knowledge of site health, safety and environmental requirements. Work Environment and Expectations Corporate office-based role within the owner’s project team, supporting mines in multiple countries. Travel to mine sites across the portfolio as required, following strict site safety rules. Close work with engineering firms, mine operations, engineers, surveyors, document controllers and contractors. A culture built on our values: Safety, Respect, Integrity, Sustainability, Excellence and Collaboration. review_candidates.title: Postdoktor i polisiärt arbete
review_candidates.description: Malmö universitet är ett öppet och nyskapande, urbant och internationellt universitet som tack vare engagerade och erfarna medarbetare bidrar till samhällsutveckling. Hos oss arbetar lärare, forskare och andra medarbetare med olika kompetenser tillsammans för att bedriva utbildning och forskning av högsta kvalitet. Alla yrkeskategorier och roller är viktiga. Du är välkommen att söka jobb hos oss! Malmö universitet är en arbetsplats och ett lärosäte som strävar efter att ha ett öppet och inkluderande synsätt, där jämställdhet och lika villkor tillför mervärde i vår verksamhet. Här kan du läsa mer om hur det är att arbeta på Malmö universitet: Jobba hos oss För dig som är internationellt sökande, läs mer här: Moving to Malmö and Sweden Vi söker Postdoktor i polisiärt arbete, till [Institutionen för polisiärt arbete, Fakulteten för hälsa och samhälle. Ämnesområde Inom ämnesområdet polisiärt arbete studeras polisen och andra aktörer med ansvar för ordning, säkerhet och trygghet i samhället. Ämnet fokuserar på polisiär och annan ordningsskapande och brottsförebyggande maktutövning, och analyserar hur dessa verksamheter organiseras, leds och genomförs, samt hur beslut fattas, hur befogenheter och professionellt omdöme används och hur metoder och kunskap omsätts i praktiken. Centralt är att undersöka och problematisera aktörernas roller, uppdrag och samverkan i det brottsbekämpande arbetet. Arbetsuppgifter Som postdoktor vid Malmö universitet ges du möjlighet att efter avlagd doktorsexamen utveckla din självständighet som forskare samt skapa förutsättning för vidare meritering. Anställningen ska huvudsakligen lämna utrymme för vetenskaplig meritering. Även undervisning kan ingå i arbetsuppgifterna, dock till högst en femtedel av arbetstiden. Inom ramen för anställningen kan även möjlighet till pedagogisk meritering och högskolepedagogisk utbildning ges. I arbetsuppgifterna ingår forskning om minst 80 % samt undervisning om max 20 % inom polisiärt arbete. Som postdoktor vid institutionen för polisiärt arbete bedriver du främst forskning med tydlig inriktning mot polisens arbete. I anställningen ingår även att planera, utveckla och genomföra undervisning, både på polisprogrammet och inom våra fristående kurser på grund- och avancerad nivå. Du förväntas bidra till utvecklingen av forsknings- och utbildningsmiljön och förväntas därför vara på plats i Malmö. Behörighetskrav Med behörighetskrav avses sådana krav som måste vara uppfyllda för att en sökande ska komma i fråga för anställning. Behörig att anställas som postdoktor är den som har avlagt doktorsexamen eller har en utländsk examen som bedöms motsvara doktorsexamen. För anställning som postdoktor är vetenskaplig skicklighet behörighetskrav. Främst bör den komma i fråga som avlagt doktorsexamen högst tre år innan tiden för ansökan för anställningen som postdoktor gått ut. Om det finns särskilda skäl kan doktorsexamen ha avlagts tidigare. Med särskilda skäl avses ledighet på grund av sjukdom, föräldraledighet, klinisk tjänstgöring, förtroendeuppdrag inom fackliga organisationer eller andra liknande omständigheter. En postdoktor får anställas tills vidare dock längst under en tid om minst två och högst tre år. Anställningen får förlängas om det finns särskilda skäl. Med särskilda skäl avses ledighet på grund av sjukdom, föräldraledighet, klinisk tjänstgöring, förtroendeuppdrag inom fackliga organisationer eller andra liknande omständigheter. En person som tidigare varit anställd vid Malmö universitet som postdoktor under mer än ett år kan inte anställas som postdoktor igen inom samma eller närliggande ämnesområde vid universitetet. Utöver dessa krav gäller som allmänt behörighetskrav att vara lämplig för och ha den förmåga i övrigt, inklusive samarbetsförmåga, som krävs för att väl fullgöra arbetsuppgifterna i denna anställning. Ytterligare Behörighetskrav För Denna Anställning Är Goda kunskaper i svenska i tal och skrift. Bedömningsgrunder Med bedömningsgrunder avses dels sådana kriterier som ligger till grund för bedömningen och hur väl en sökande uppfyller ett visst behörighetskrav, dels sådana kriterier som i övrigt har bedömts ska ha betydelse för anställningen. Vid anställning som postdoktor ska vetenskaplig skicklighet främst beaktas. Den samlade bedömningen ska också omfatta pedagogisk skicklighet, samverkansskicklighet samt akademiskt medborgarskap, ledarskap och administrativ skicklighet. Bedömningsgrunder För Vetenskaplig Skicklighet Är forskning inom områden med relevans för den aktuella anställningen, aktiv delaktighet och god förankring i vetenskapssamhället, förmåga att initiera, planera, utveckla, självständigt genomföra och leda forskning av hög kvalitet och med internationellt genomslag och betydande omfattning, förmåga till internationella forskningssamarbeten, förmåga att attrahera externa forskningsmedel i konkurrens med hänsyn tagen till ämnesområdets särart och tradition, förmåga att tillämpa principer för öppen vetenskap, samt förmåga att kommunicera forskning inom och utom vetenskapssamhället. För denna anställning är följande bedömningsgrund av särskild betydelse: forskning inom områden med relevans för den aktuella anställningen. review_candidates.title: Disability and Inclusion Consultant
review_candidates.description: Application Closing Date 6th of November Context of Role WISH 2 (Women’s Integrated Sexual Health) is one of three components of the overarching WISH Dividend programme that is being procured by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO). This programme is central to delivering the UK’s priorities on empowering women and girls as set out in the International Development Strategy, the UK’s strategic approach to sub-Saharan Africa and the International Women and Girls Strategy. IPPF is the prime contractor on Lot 2 – Eastern and Southern Africa covering the following countries: Burundi, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Zambia. During the implementation years, the WISH2 program will ensure that transformative approaches for disability inclusion are mainstreamed throughout the programme and national healthcare systems. Role Purpose The consultant will provide technical support to the WISH2 programme, with a focus on accelerating the implementation of WISH2 disability and inclusion strategy especially, policy and systems interventions across the WISH2 countries. The consultant will provide tailored support to WISH2 consortium partners, Organisations of People with Disabilities (OPDs), and accountability mechanisms at country level. Technical Assistance (TA) will focus on capacity building, course correction, capitalization and sustainability of interventions across outputs, strengthening mainstreaming of disability inclusion in healthcare systems. Deliverables Through tailored technical assistance, the consultant will support the following key activities. The consultant will: Guide the multi-stakeholder reflection on findings from the recently concluded disability marker (self-assessment), and document lessons learned. Review the facility disability audit findings, prioritised disability inclusion activities and provide comprehensive recommendations for course correction, scaling, capitalisation and institutionalisation of adopted disability inclusive approaches. Review the OPD capacity assessment data, develop a capacity building framework adapted to needs and contextual considerations, and enable cross-country learning and exchange. Support the design and implementation of the OPD sub-granting mechanism including reviewing proposals, contributing to developing Technical Assistance Agreement (TAA), and providing tailored TA at implementation phase. Collaborate with the WISH2 MERL team on the disability research and learning agendas, including disability measurement study, and contributing to development and review of learning products. Review national policy/strategic priorities identified in country workplans and Country Policy Overview and Engagement plans (CPOEP) and provide TA to ensure they are progressing and aligned to the latest evidence, best practices and inclusive health systems strengthening approaches. Building on the already established OPD database and relationships, establish a community of practice for WISH2 ESA, to facilitate learning, amplify voices and bolster empowerment among OPDs, CSOs and partners. Review the safeguarding pilot model for Zambia to strengthen inclusion of people with disabilities and their needs in the model guideline, training materials, and implementation phase. Tools and approaches The Consultant Will Adapt And Apply WISH2’s Tools And Approaches To Meet Programme Goals. WISH2’s Disability Inclusion Strategy Puts Disability Rights Across All Its Work And Promotes Safe, Inclusive Conditions And Meaningful Participation Within Healthcare Systems. It Uses a Twin-track Approach Mainstreaming: build disability inclusion into all policies, programming and service delivery, so people with disabilities can access and benefit from SRH services. Targeted interventions: address specific physical and attitudinal barriers through tailored SBC outreach, accessible SRH information, reasonable accommodation, assistive support, and involvement of organisations of persons with disabilities (OPDs). Tools such as the Disability Inclusion Marker and Disability Audit tools will be adapted to each country, including humanitarian settings, in consultation with WISH2 staff and national stakeholders. Contracting approach The contractual model is a draw-down contract, whereby each specific assignment will be agreed in advance with the contract manager (Deputy Director, Technical WISH2). For each new task/assignment, a new work order will be prepared. The total number of days will not exceed 60 days over the 5-month duration of the framework contract. Both parties will discuss and agree on the details for each assignment, including the necessary timeframes and deadlines. This will be defined in writing via a Work Order. At the point of each work order, deliverables will be determined and agreed. The Work Order will describe payment and approval mechanisms as well as the outputs required for the assignment. The consultancy rate/remuneration will be subjected to Kenya withholding tax. Essential Skills Postgraduate university degree in gender, social or natural sciences or other relevant disciplines. Significant demonstratable experience in disability inclusion and disability rights in health, including the twin-track approach (mainstreaming plus targeted interventions) for international development programmes. Experience with disability inclusion for Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights programmes funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) is highly preferred. Strong knowledge of SRHR and health systems in Africa, including sub-national and facility-level service delivery. Experience developing, adapting and contextualizing disability inclusion tools, such as disability inclusion markers and accessibility or disability audits, for different countries and humanitarian settings. Skill in SBCC and demand creation that addresses harmful social and gender norms, with accessible information formats. Understanding disability-disaggregated data: collection, analysis and use for decisions (for example the Washington Group question sets). Familiarity with inclusive policy, financing and accountability processes, and with national and regional frameworks such as the CRPD and the Maputo Protocol. Capacity strengthening experience including training, mentoring and coaching of health providers, programme teams and partners. Participatory facilitation and stakeholder engagement, including working with organisations of persons with disabilities (OPDs), ministries of health, CSOs and technical working groups. Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively with people from different countries and cultures. Fluent in English. Additional working proficiency in French preferred (verbal and written) Strong analytical and research skills. Excellent time management and organizational skills. Desirable Skills Application Process Please send your CV and cover letter detailing your experience and why you are best suited for the consultancy and send to email address ippfarbids@ippf.org with the subject heading “Disability and Inclusion Consultant” Deadline for application is 6th of November 2026 (Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to submit your application early). By joining IPPF, you become part of a mission-driven organization dedicated to empowering individuals and communities, advancing gender equality, and improving access to comprehensive healthcare services. Bringing Positive Change: IPPF brings positive change to the lives of millions of people worldwide. Reducing maternal mortality, preventing unintended pregnancies, combating gender-based violence, promoting comprehensive sexuality education, and advocating for the realization of sexual and reproductive health, rights and justice for all, and especially marginalized people. Supportive of people’s rights regardless of sexuality or gender identity/expression and supportive of workers’ rights and access to health care in sex work.
